tools.name: resource_reference
tools.description: Discover OCI policy resource types and families from names, aliases or everyday wording (for example virtual machines). Returns canonical catalog identifiers, documented source spellings, family membership and cumulative allow-verb permissions. Use before policy_search when the resource name is uncertain. Empty or unavailable mappings are explicit; no tenancy load or OCI API call is needed. Results describe bundled reference data, not access decisions.

query.description: Resource/family identifier, alias or everyday wording.

PermissionExpansion.description: A bounded cumulative permission list, with an explicit total and truncation.

ResourceReferenceMatch.description: Resource/family identity, membership and cumulative allow-verb expansion.

outputSchema.description: Structured resource discovery and expansion result.

tools.name: operation_reference
tools.description: Discover OCI API operation names and their catalog permission requirements. Returns qualified identities such as core:LaunchInstance, request.operation values, conditional notes, related checks and unmapped permissions. Bare operation names can match multiple API groups; do not choose silently. Use before permission lookup or simulation. Bundled catalog only; no OCI calls.

query.description: Qualified/bare API name or discovery wording.

OperationReferenceMatch.description: Qualified API identity, known requirements and unresolved resource mappings.

RelatedReferenceCheck.description: Conditional or related API requirements retained from the catalog.

tools.name: permission_reference
tools.description: Find OCI permission names and reverse-map them to known resources, families, lowest granting allow verbs and API operations. Search a partial permission or use match=exact. Additional permissions show the broader grant at that verb; this is not a complete least-privilege policy plan. Operation-only permissions remain visible when resource mapping is unavailable. No tenancy load, OCI calls or authorization decisions.

query.description: Permission identifier or partial permission wording.

PermissionExpansion.description: A bounded cumulative permission list, with an explicit total and truncation.

PermissionReferenceMatch.description: Permission evidence from resource tables and operation requirements.

PermissionResourceMatch.description: Lowest catalog granting verb for one resource, not a complete policy plan.

outputSchema.description: Structured permission discovery and reverse mapping result.

tools.name: policy_search
tools.description: Search OCI IAM policies for one question. For two or more related checks, comparisons across groups/services, or a deployment permission checklist, prefer policy_search_set in one call. Principal filters: use filters.principal for one structured selector (for example {"principal_type":"group","domain_name":"Default","name":"Admins"} or {"principal_type":"dynamic-group"}), filters.principals for OR selectors, and filters.principal_keys for exact canonical keys such as group:default/admins (mixed-case inputs are accepted). Resource values are OCI policy types, not product names. Use resource_reference to discover resource names before searching when uncertain. For "which groups can manage Object Storage", use filters.action=["allow"], filters.principal={"principal_type":"group"}, filters.verb=["manage"], and filters.resource_family="object storage". This expands to buckets, objects, objectstorage-namespaces, object-family, and all-resources. Results are matching statements, not a proof of effective access; conditions and scope still matter. The limit is a detailed-row threshold capped at 50, not pagination. Unfiltered or larger results return a summary with summary_substituted, summary_reason, and a hint to narrow the filters instead of statement rows.

MCPPolicyFilters.description: Discoverable common policy filters, with additional legacy fields retained.

action.description: Statement actions. Use ["allow"] when asking which identities are granted access.

principal.description: One structured identity selector, such as {"principal_type":"group"}.

principals.description: Alternative identity selectors; any one may match.

verb.description: OCI IAM policy verbs. Values are exact matches; multiple values are alternatives.

resource.description: OCI policy resource type identifiers, not service names. Values are alternatives. For Object Storage, use buckets, objects, objectstorage-namespaces, object-family, and all-resources; or use resource_family="object storage" to include that full scope.

resource_family.description: Reference-data family name or alias. For example, "object storage" expands to buckets, objects, objectstorage-namespaces, object-family, and all-resources.

MCPPrincipalSelector.description: One identity selector; populated fields are matched together.

principal_type.description: Identity kind, such as group, dynamic-group, resource-principal, or instance-principal.

limit.description: Detailed-row threshold, 1-50. Broader results become a summary; not pagination.

tools.name: policy_search_set
tools.description: Run multiple related OCI policy queries in one call and compare their coverage. Prefer this tool over repeated policy_search calls when the question asks about two or more groups, services, human versus workload permissions, or a product/deployment permission checklist. Supply one searches item per check with search_id, label and filters (same fields as policy_search, including resource_family and structured principals). Use detail_level="summary" for comparisons. Use intent="access_review" for access comparisons, "install_validation" for a permission checklist, or "workload_analysis" for workload checks. product_or_service is a label, not a search filter. Returns search_results per check and set_summary with missing_required_searches and coverage caveats. Matches and likely_ready are statement evidence, not proof of effective access or installation readiness. Legacy items with query:{...} are still accepted. For a single lookup use policy_search.

detail_level.description: Use summary for comparisons; simple/full for bounded statement evidence.
